note: Tars's shelf: short passages about the chart room, each with an id Tars cites. Written from the package logs in handover/packages (named in each passage's from). Keep each passage short and true to what is built; add one when a screen ships.

passages.title: The chart
passages.text: The Chart screen draws the system as a chart: the star, each world on its orbit, moons as ticks. Click a body or press Tab to reach it, then Enter to select it; its card shows its facts. In edit mode you type a new value on the card or drag a body to move its orbit. Distances are on a log scale. Every edit is a dated, authored event in the campaign's history, so Ctrl+Z undoes it as a new correction.

passages.title: Why does a value have this value?
passages.text: Every derived value has a why? link. It explains the value at three depths: Curious (no background assumed), Science (the mechanism and its assumptions) and Engine (ids, versions, determinism), with the references the physics is built on. Open the flow puts that value's physics on the bench on the Physics screen.

passages.title: Changing the physics
passages.text: The Physics screen shows a physics flow as blocks joined by wires, with the selected body's real values. Type a new parameter on a block to draft a change request. The kernel checks it before it can be adopted; the panel shows the change, its effect on the body and that it applies to every body the flow serves. Adopt puts it in the campaign's own physics pack; Withdraw takes it back out. Changed values carry a changed physics stamp.

passages.title: Lenses
passages.text: A lens decides what the chart draws, what each card shows and which tools are on the bar: Basic, Advanced, Building, Running, and every player data view as seen by the players. Make your own from the Lens menu. Switching lens never changes data, time or the selection. Honesty marks (authored, impossible, fictional, changed physics) always show to the GM.

passages.title: What players can see
passages.text: The Player data screen holds the data views: what each audience is shown of each body, and when. The Scanned button grants a body's scanned view to an audience; a second press takes it back. Unscanned facts show as not yet scanned on the players' screens. Secrets such as GM notes never reach a player scene.

passages.title: Sharing with players
passages.text: Share with players opens a session that players join from their own devices, peer to peer. The GM's machine is the only writer: players see the scenes their seat may see and send requests the GM approves. If the GM goes offline, players stay read only on the last snapshot. The Switchboard holds the roles: each role card sets what that role knows (fog of war, its own knowledge, or another role's), its layout, links and brand.

passages.title: The time ruler
passages.text: The ruler at the bottom shows the system's history and what may come. Drag the marker or use the arrow keys to move through time; the chart shows the system as it was or will be. Events such as oceans forming are marked on it. Futures in italics are one plausible future, not a fixed one.

passages.title: What if
passages.text: What if opens a branch of the campaign's history where you edit freely without touching the main line. Keep folds the branch back in; Drop throws it away.

passages.title: Look ahead: ageing a system
passages.text: Look ahead ages the system on a branch: the star evolves on its life line and the orbits change slowly over time. Scrub through the result, then keep it or throw it away. A run to a cold white dwarf is heavy work; weaker devices take longer.

passages.title: Making or importing a system
passages.text: Make a system imports a Star System Explorer 3 save, with a report of what was carried over, or grows a new system through the formation pipeline. Both show a preview first; Add to the campaign adopts it as history.

passages.title: A body's globe and cutaway
passages.text: The Body screen shows the selected world as a globe drawn from its surface tiles, and a cutaway of its layers from core to sky, read from the kernel's world stack.

passages.title: Comparing sizes and measuring
passages.text: The Sizes screen lines bodies up at true scale: from this system, the campaign and reference objects such as Earth and Jupiter. Measure on the chart gives the distance between two points.

passages.title: Life
passages.text: The Life screen shows a world's life: its epochs, its food web of guilds, and what can be detected of it at each scan tier, in three lenses. Life is resolved from the world's energy and chemistry, never painted on.

passages.title: Packs
passages.text: Packs add physics, game rules, universes and looks, stacked in order. Each kind of thing has exactly one publisher in the stack, and a pack that changes another's flow says so explicitly. Fictional physics is labelled fictional.

passages.title: Player screens and themes
passages.text: Player screens are documents you compose from views (chart, card, table, text, readout) and dress with a theme, such as green phosphor or a starship panel. Styles hold each view's settings; Symbols choose diagrammatic or colour-coded marks. Orac can draft any of these from a sentence.

passages.title: Light
passages.text: Light switches how the chart is coloured: as the eye sees it, as a camera would, or astronomy palettes and single bands. A label says which is in use. Some spectra are still stand-ins and say so.

passages.title: Sound
passages.text: Sound is off until you turn it on. When on, it plays sound only where sound can exist, with captions.

passages.title: Saving the campaign
passages.text: The campaign is kept in this browser after every change. Save writes it to a file; Open reads one back; Start fresh begins again. Players can join a reopened campaign.

passages.title: Agents and keys
passages.text: Tars, Orac and Minerva run on your own model: link a provider (OpenRouter with one key, LM Studio or Ollama on this computer, or another by its /v1 address) and link a model to each job. Keys stay in this browser and go only to their own provider. Every run shows its estimate first and its cost after, within a daily cap. Everything else works with no agent linked.

passages.title: Orac
passages.text: Orac drafts changes from a sentence: physics changes, lenses, styles, player screens, symbologies, data views, programs (autopilots for program seats), object templates (what a made object starts with and which programs it may run), triggers (when this happens, do that), story sifters, boxes (several physics blocks used as one), game tables (a rule-book lookup turned into classes worked out from physics), missing gases and substances for the data sheet (invented ones marked fictional), and new physics blocks as issues. SSE checks every draft and sends problems back to Orac up to three times. Only drafts that pass can be accepted, and nothing changes until you accept. Orac's physics changes are filed on the Physics screen for you to adopt.

passages.title: Minerva
passages.text: Minerva writes narrative for one audience from what that audience knows. Every number she writes must be in their facts, and what they have not been shown stays out.

passages.title: Device tiers
passages.text: The status line shows this device's tier, measured from how much work it does per second. Heavy work such as ageing a system runs on capable devices; a weaker device does less and says where its edge is.

passages.title: Authored, impossible and fictional marks
passages.text: Values the GM typed are marked authored. Edits physics says cannot happen are allowed but marked impossible. Values from fictional physics are marked fictional. The GM always sees these marks; players see them only if their data view shows them.
